newsitem.title: POLAND: ZLOTY SLIPS LOWER VS BASKET, SMALL REBOUND SEEN.
newsitem.headline: ZLOTY SLIPS LOWER VS BASKET, SMALL REBOUND SEEN.

text.p: The Polish zloty continued its recent downward drift on Thursday as bank's rebuilt positions and currency-buying importer orders pulled the local unit lower in heavy turnover, dealers said.
But they said the zloty's three-day slide may run out of steam on Friday as some foreign currency speculators were keen on taking zloty positions if the Polish unit lost more ground.

"The recent zloty softening has created a good level to open longer (zloty) positions and some foreign investors may be buying the Polish currency if it slips further," said Piotr Czyzewski, forex dealer at ING Bank in Warsaw.
The zloty closed at minus 1.13/1.18 percent from the parity rate, against Wednesday's minus 0.86/0.94 percent.
It closed at 3.5095/10 to the dollar, against 3.5020/60 on Wednesday and at 1.8685/95 to the mark, against 1.8545/60.
Dealers said that any zloty rebound should stop well short of resistance around minus 0.5 percent.
"Foreign buying may lift the zloty a little, but it is not likely to rise to -0.5 percent from parity," one dealer said.
Dealers said that many longer-term foreign investors would continue to stay away from Polish treasuries before parliamentary elections on September 21.
On the money market one-day rates closed stradling 23 percent, seen by dealers as the new balance level after Monday's official interest rate rise.
Overnight rates closed at 22.90/23.20 percent, against Wednesday's 22.80/23.30 and tomorrow/next rates were at 22.90/23.25, against yesterday's 22.80/23.30.
The central bank again refrained from staging any open market operations. It last set its benchmark 14-day reverse repo rate at 23.00 percent.
